title: Generic Methods
concept: Methods on types can have their own type parameters, separate from any type-level generics — enabling methods like map and and_then.
why: Without generic methods, each operation returning a different type would need a separate implementation. Generic methods enable flexible transformations.
tips: Method-level type params are independent of type-level params — use different letters
Generic methods are powerful for chaining: opt.map(f).and_then(g).unwrap_or(h)
The caller specifies method type params: w.transform[Str](f)
Methods can have both type-level AND method-level constraints
common_mistakes: Shadowing the type-level T with a method-level T — use different letters
Forgetting that the method needs type annotations from the caller
Using method-level generics when the type-level param would suffice — keep it simple
